title: Microscopic Evaluation of Temperature Effects on Gelatin Support Bath for 3D Bioprinting
content: Freeform reversible embedding of suspended hydrogels (FRESH) is a 3D bioprinting technique that utilizes a thermoreversible support bath to enable the precise arrangement of hydrogels into complex biological frameworks [1]. Unlike traditional 3D printing methods that rely on solid support structures, FRESH printing utilizes a reversible, soft support material like gelatin to suspend a hydrogel, such as sodium alginate, during the printing process. Since the hydrogel is unable to maintain its shape independently during printing, the gelatin holds up the structure in real time, preserving the desired configuration and greatly enhancing feature fidelity. The gelatin microparticles function as a Bingham plastic during the printing process, remaining rigid under low shear stresses but flowing as a viscous fluid when subjected to higher shear stresses [2]. For successful slurry preparation, previous studies emphasized the importance of slurry temperature during stirring, while recommending different specific temperatures of 20°C up to 25°C [1-5]. To the best of our knowledge, there have been no reports on how gelatin microparticle morphology changes based on preparation within this narrow temperature range, or the impact microparticle morphology has on effective FRESH printing. The goal of the study is to characterize gelatin slurry at 25°C compared to ambient room temperature air to determine the effects of slurry temperature during stirring on the microparticle morphology and printed hydrogels.
